title: Assessing High-Risk AI Systems under the EU AI Act: From Legal Requirements to Technical Verification
explain_beginner: The European Union's AI Act sets rules for high-risk artificial intelligence systems, but companies and regulators weren't sure how to actually check if AI systems followed these rules. This paper creates a practical guide that breaks down the legal requirements into specific, testable activities that can be checked at different stages of building and running AI systems. It helps everyone understand and verify compliance in the same way.
explain_business: Companies deploying high-risk AI systems in Europe now have a clear, standardized methodology for demonstrating compliance with the AI Act. This framework reduces legal uncertainty, enables consistent audits across regions, and provides a reusable compliance roadmap that works regardless of AI technology type. Organizations can use this to streamline their compliance programs, reduce assessment costs, and demonstrate regulatory readiness to authorities and stakeholders.
explain_practitioner: We systematically decomposed EU AI Act articles into operational sub-requirements grounded in established standards and practices. We then mapped these requirements to concrete verification activities characterized by verification type and lifecycle stage. The resulting framework translates high-level regulatory obligations into implementable, technology-agnostic assessment procedures across the full AI development cycle, reducing ambiguity in compliance interpretation and enabling consistent, auditable verification processes.
